Patient class timing helpers for link_encounters()

Source: R/utils-link-encounters.R
parse_mdt_updates.Rd

Internal helpers that decide the chronological order of an episode's patient classes and which row represents the episode.

Usage

parse_mdt_updates(mdt_str, n_classes)

parse_mdt_segment(seg, n_classes)

safe_as_posixct(x)

episode_class_sequence(episode, patient_class, class_time)

pick_primary_row_index(patient_classes)

episode_primary_row(episode, patient_class)

Arguments

mdt_str

A single C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates string (may be NA or empty).

n_classes

Integer. The number of patient classes in the corresponding C_Patient_Class_List value.

seg

A single trimmed, non-empty C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates segment.

x

A vector of timestamps, as character or anything coercible with as.character(). A POSIXct vector is returned unchanged.

episode

Vector identifying the episode each row belongs to (for example .episode_id); rows with equal values are one episode.

patient_class

Character vector of one episode's patient classes, one per row (so a class can repeat).

class_time

POSIXct vector, parallel to patient_class, of the time each row's class occurred (NA where unknown).

patient_classes

Character vector of an episode's patient classes, one per row.

Value

parse_mdt_updates() returns a character vector of length n_classes. parse_mdt_segment() returns a list with idx (an integer position) and time (a string), or NULL. safe_as_posixct() returns a POSIXct vector the length of x. episode_class_sequence() returns a character vector the length of episode: each row's episode sequence, NA for an episode with no non-missing patient class. pick_primary_row_index() returns a single integer. episode_primary_row() returns a logical vector the length of episode, TRUE on each episode's primary row.

Details

parse_mdt_updates() parses ESSENCE's C_Patient_Class_MDT_Updates encoding: pipe-delimited {position};timestamp; segments, one per patient class, where position is the 1-based character position in the corresponding C_Patient_Class_List value (for example {1};2026-06-19 16:00:06.000;|{2};2026-06-19 17:55:10.000; for C_Patient_Class_List = "EI"). It returns a character vector of length n_classes holding the timestamp string at each position, NA where no segment matches that position (for example a class that was never explicitly updated) or the segment does not match this encoding.

safe_as_posixct() parses timestamps for chronological ordering. A single malformed or non-standard value must not abort the whole vectorized parse (as.POSIXct() throws rather than warns when a string matches none of its tryFormats), so values that cannot be parsed become NA and ordering degrades gracefully to the next tier for just that row instead of failing link_encounters() entirely. It recognizes space- and T-separated ISO 8601-style timestamps (with or without a trailing Z) and US-style month/day/year timestamps, trying each format against the whole vector at once and keeping the first format that parses each element.

episode_class_sequence() orders each episode's distinct patient classes by the earliest class_time each class occurs at, for example "Direct Admit->ED" when the direct-admit record's timestamp precedes the ED record's, and returns that string for every row of the episode. It falls back to alphabetical order when no usable timestamp exists for the episode at all; classes with no timestamp sort after timed classes when some but not all classes in the episode have one. Classes with identical timestamps (every class derived from one record shares that record's timestamp) also fall back to alphabetical order. That is a tiebreak only: when the timestamps are missing or equal the true order cannot be determined from the data, so the alphabetical order carries no clinical meaning.

parse_mdt_segment() parses one trimmed, non-empty {position};timestamp; segment into its position and timestamp string, or returns NULL when the segment does not match this encoding or its position is not between 1 and n_classes.

pick_primary_row_index() returns the index of the ED row in an episode if one exists, else 1 (the first row in original order): the row whose values represent the episode when it is collapsed. episode_primary_row() marks that row in every episode of a long-format data frame, which is what .index_encounter records, so a long-format count of index encounters always equals the number of rows in the collapsed output.
